label: Crash loop
definition: An isolate or the bus worker that keeps crashing, and the limits that stop it restarting forever.

label: Restart
definition: Starting an isolate, a pool or the bus worker again after a crash, a hang or on request.

label: Heartbeat
definition: The periodic beat a worker sends, and the lag and busy time measured from it.

label: Blocked worker
definition: A worker whose event loop stops answering, and how it's detected, killed or simulated.

label: Bus restart
definition: What happens to isolates, topics and publishes when the bus worker crashes and comes back.

label: Back-pressure
definition: Limits that stop a fast producer or reader from swamping a slow one: credit, backlog, caps and buffers.

label: Delivery guarantees
definition: How many times a record reaches a subscriber, in what order, and what happens when one is lost.

label: Offsets and commits
definition: How a reader records which records it has settled, and where it resumes from.

label: Replay
definition: Reading a topic's retained history again: on subscribe, after a wake, after a restart.

label: Retention
definition: How much of a topic's log is kept, and what a reader sees when records age out.

label: Durability
definition: Keeping a topic's log across a bus crash, a page reload or a discarded tab.

label: Memory topics
definition: Topics whose log lives only in the bus worker's memory, and what they lose.

label: Grants
definition: Permissions in an isolate's manifest: which topics it may read or write and which host calls it may make.

label: Trust boundary
definition: What isolate code can and can't reach: sanitising, untrusted events, tokens, shared realms.

label: Schemas and validation
definition: How topic values are described, validated and stored as the schema's output.

label: Migration
definition: Moving data or code across a breaking change: topic versions, seeds and codemods.

label: Compatibility
definition: Which versions of the host, the isolates and the formats work together.

label: Pools
definition: Several isolates sharing one worker, and what they share as a result.

label: Placement
definition: Where an isolate runs (its own worker, a pool, a balancer pool) and how it moves.

label: Suspension
definition: Stopping idle isolates to free memory, and waking them when needed.

label: Lifecycle
definition: The steps of an isolate's or the kernel's life: start, ready, stop, shutdown.

label: Timeouts and windows
definition: Every time limit a rule sets: timeouts, windows, intervals and cooldowns.

label: Measurement
definition: How load, memory and time are measured, and what the numbers are for.

label: Memory use
definition: How much memory workers and isolates cost, and how it's measured.

label: Budgets and caps
definition: Hard and soft limits on counts and sizes: worker budgets, caps, bundle budgets.

label: Frameworks
definition: How React, Preact and other UI frameworks plug in through adapters and hooks.

label: Rendering
definition: How a worker-side DOM reaches the page: records, the applier and the compositor.

label: Main thread
definition: What runs on the page's main thread, and what is kept off it.

label: Host API
definition: What the app's host code calls on the kernel.

label: Request and reply
definition: Asking an isolate for an answer through a requestable topic.

label: Keys
definition: Per-key values on a topic: keyed records, watches per key, the null key.

label: Observability
definition: Seeing inside a running app: the inspection feed, devtools, events and metrics.

label: Development only
definition: Behaviour that exists only in development builds or tools.

label: Browser differences
definition: Where Chromium, Firefox and WebKit behave differently, and the baseline Isoloop needs.

label: Tabs
definition: Behaviour across several tabs of the same app.

label: Error codes
definition: Rules that define an error code an API rejects or throws with.

label: Own the stack
definition: Places where Isoloop builds its own piece instead of taking a library or platform feature.

label: Releases
definition: How versions are numbered, staged, approved, tagged and supported.

label: CI checks
definition: What continuous integration checks on a pull request, on main and at night.

label: Source layout
definition: How packages, entries and source folders are organised.

label: Build toolchain
definition: The tools the repo builds, lints, formats and tests with.

label: Reserved names
definition: Names and prefixes the runtime keeps for itself, and what happens if an app uses one.
